title: BALMS: Benchmarking Agentic LLMs for Longitudinal Mental Health Sensing
abstract: arXiv:2608.27219v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Mental health assessment relies on episodic self-report scales, which convert subjective states such as stress into numerical scores but provide only sparse snapshots of wellbeing. Wearable devices offer longitudinal behavioral and physiological signals for continuous, low-burden monitoring. Recent LLM-driven personal-health agents enable natural language queries over wearable signals, but mainly handle short-term, retrieval-based lookups (e.g., highest step count over a week). They do not evaluate whether agents can reason over long-term signals to predict wellbeing scores paired with evidence-grounded rationales. translated_title: BALMS：面向纵向心理健康感知的智能体大语言模型基准测试
translated_abstract: 心理健康评估依赖于偶发性的自我报告量表，这些量表将压力等主观状态转化为数值分数，但仅能提供稀疏的健康状况快照。可穿戴设备提供纵向的行为和生理信号，用于连续、低负担的监测。近年来，由大语言模型驱动的个人健康智能体能够对可穿戴信号进行自然语言查询，但主要处理短期的、基于检索的查询（例如，一周内的最高步数）。它们并未评估智能体是否能对长期信号进行推理，以预测与基于证据的推理相匹配的健康分数。为解决这一空白，我们引入了BALMS，这是首个针对纵向心理健康感知的基于大语言模型的智能体系统的系统性基准测试。BALMS涵盖3个真实世界的纵向数据集、2个任务族（封闭式健康分数预测和由大语言模型作为评判者自动评分的推理生成）、3种智能体范式评估。
tldr: 该论文提出了BALMS，这是首个针对纵向心理健康感知的智能体大语言模型基准测试，旨在评估智能体对长期信号推理并预测健康分数及生成基于证据推理的能力。
en_tdlr: This paper introduces BALMS, the first systematic benchmark for agentic LLMs in longitudinal mental health sensing, evaluating agents' ability to reason over long-term signals and predict wellbeing scores with evidence-grounded rationales.
